newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh central bank assured autonomy -- governor.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh central bank assured autonomy -- governor.

text.p: The Bangladesh government, pursuing sweeping financial reforms, has agreed not to dilute the autonomy of the central bank, Bangladesh Bank governor Lutfar Rahman Sarkar said on Monday.
"In fact we (central bank) already have full autonomy in black and white, but this has not been exercised in the past," he told Reuters.
"The present government has, in consultation with us, agreed that it would not interfere with (our) autonomy," Sarkar said without elaborating.
He was responding to concern expressed by the World Bank that the Bangladesh Bank lacked authority to formulate and implement reforms in the financial sector.
"We are doing everything possible to break out of the stagnancy and implement reforms quicker in pursuance of the government policies," Sarkar said.
"To ensure the efficiency and autonomy of the central bank, we have forwarded a proposal to the government and the government has accepted it," he said but gave no details.
The World Bank, in a recent report to the Bangladeshi government, made several suggestions to strengthen banking.
They included increasing Bangladesh Bank's supervision and enforcement powers, legal action against loan defaulters and a programme of restructuring and privatising nationalised commercial banks.
The report, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, said financial sector reforms in Bangladesh had been "worst hit" during the past government.

"More than the economy, it was structural reforms that stalled in Financial Year '96 (July-June). Of the three key reform components -- private sector development, public sector reform, and human development -- the first two slowed the most. Banking reform and privatisation were the worst hit," the report said.
"Politics and policy slippages in FY 96 combined to muddy Bangladesh's good record of macroeconomic stability, although the negative impact turned out to be less than expected."
But the report had some praise for the country's current government headed by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who took over in June.
"The new government has enunciated its development vision quickly," the report said.
"It has emphasised firm commitment to poverty reduction, social justice, and structural reforms aimed at reaching 7 percent GDP (Gross Domestic Product) growth led by the private sector."
